Two regjeringen.no pages returned 403; their content comes via search snippets.

Access path: Unauthenticated pre-auth OS command injection (CVE-2026-1731) in outdated, internet-facing Bomgar/BeyondTrust Remote Support instances run by an MSP and a dental software vendor. Access path: Unauthenticated admin takeover of internet-facing N-central servers (CVE-2026-18577, bypass of CVE-2026-18556 fix), exploited from 31 Jul 2026; attackers then used built-in Take Control remote sessions to reach managed devices and installed Cloudflare tunnels to keep access.

Coding notes: [E179] Beget says no attempts to download or modify user data were seen, so Exfiltration is N and Data exposed is N. Binary VPS backups were fully lost; the cause was not stated. No customer count, and no group claim confirmed. A follow-on DDoS peaked at 2.1 Tbit/s. NKTsKI and police were involved. The management-platform boundary fits better; 'Service provider holding customer data' is the secondary option.

Incident: FirstVDS (Russian VPS hosting provider): an HTTP Request Smuggling flaw in ISPsystem VMmanager 6 was used to run a stealer on hypervisor nodes, which mounted customer VM disks read-only and exfiltrated credentials and files (October 2026)
Access path: The attacker exploited an HTTP Request Smuggling flaw (CL.0, smuggled inside a WebSocket handshake) in the internet-facing VMmanager 6 panel to get admin rights. The panel's own task mechanism then ran a stealer on hypervisor nodes. The stealer mounted client VM disks read-only, collected selected files and sent the archives to an attacker server.
Orgs reached (as reported): FirstVDS did not disclose how many customers were affected. Its postmortem reports stealer archives on 457 hypervisor nodes, which are shared by many customers' VMs. ISPsystem declined to disclose the number of affected operators.
Coding notes: [E181] FirstVDS says the stealer changed nothing on VM disks and reports no wiping, so Ransomware is N. Account creation is N because FirstVDS found no rogue panel accounts. The Bpfit/Gsnetcat backdoors and disguised hidden services support Services/tasks. Shell is Y on 'suspicious scripts'. The 117 GiB archive total is not a confirmed exfiltrated volume. No NKTsKI or Roskomnadzor statement was found. The ISPsystem source is a ComNews-hosted statement.
People or orgs exposed: Customers not counted; 457 hypervisor nodes (FirstVDS postmortem, late Oct 2026)

Incident: AOMEI Backupper update-server tampering (UNC7017): attackers briefly altered AOMEI's remote config files (down_html.ini, Notifycfg.ini) in 5–10 minute windows between April and July 2026, so Backupper clients downloaded and ran the CROSSROAD dropper, which installed a modified Radmin, the SHINYROAD backdoor and later Adaptix C2. One window also forced NetNTLMv2 hash leakage. Disclosed 16–19 Oct 2026.
Access path: Compromise of the vendor's update server. Unauthenticated remote config files were altered to redirect the download to a malicious upgrade-now.zip with a matching MD5, and the promotional-popup channel forced it to run. Original files were restored after each window.
Orgs reached (as reported): ManageEngine: 2 unrelated organisations in different countries (28 May 2026 detections). GTIG/Mandiant: victims notified in IT services, telecommunications and higher education across 11 countries (AU, BR, IN, PK, PT, SG, ZA, ES, CH, TR, US), no count given. AOMEI: no count, still assessing.
Coding notes: [E183] ManageEngine confirms 2 orgs; GTIG's 11-country spread implies more, but no count, so reach is Unknown (more than one). Credential access is NTLM coercion only (T1187); AOMEI says exposure is unconfirmed. ManageEngine says Radmin was staged, not armed, with no new account. Malware aborts on security agents but does not disable them. Google says AnyViewer was also hit; AOMEI disputes it.
People or orgs exposed: 2 organisations (ManageEngine, 16 Oct 2026); GTIG victims in 11 countries, count not given (16 Oct 2026)

Access path: Attacker registered a trial account with a false identity, got command execution on OpsShield's billing and licensing server (manage.opsshield.com), then used a stolen access key to upload a fake cPGuard update (versions 5.88.12-5.88.19) to the update CDN. From 02:08 to 03:20 UTC on 2 Nov 2026, agents that polled for updates ran it as root on customer hosting servers.
Orgs reached (as reported): About 2,950 customer servers ran the fake update (OpsShield estimate). An earlier notice said files were confirmed retrieved from 32 customer servers. About 7,900 billing-portal client records were copied (OpsShield). No count of affected organisations was given.
Coding notes: [E186] Figures changed: the first notice reported 32 confirmed exfiltrated files, a later one about 2,950 servers. Organisation count unknown, so band rests on servers plus 7,900 client records. Lateral movement was inside OpsShield's systems only. The payload added a setuid root shell and cron job, not accounts. Exfil destination differs between notices. Pre-assigned values kept.
People or orgs exposed: About 2,950 customer servers and about 7,900 client records (OpsShield disclosure, Nov 2026)

Incident: TeamUpdraft breach (Oct 2026): stolen UpdraftCentral Cloud connection keys used to send signed remote commands that installed backdoor plugins and created privileged accounts on connected WordPress sites
Access path: Attacker got into teamupdraft.com over 17-18 Oct 2026 and probably reached the customer database, which held UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone connection keys. Using the stolen dashboard keys, the attacker sent validly signed UpdraftCentral remote-management commands (plugin.upload_plugin, plugin.delete_plugin) to connected sites. These installed backdoor plugins that create Editor+/admin accounts or log in as existing admins.
Orgs reached (as reported): No confirmed total. TeamUpdraft gives no count (only 'a small number of cases' of sites compromised in the original incident, 29 Oct update). Patchstack saw 99 distinct backdoor plugin names 'across a broad set of sites' (18 Oct 15:32 to 19 Oct 09:23). Nethemba confirmed 2 of its own 3 targeted sites backdoored. Potential exposure of up to about 400,000 sites (under 10% of 4M+ installs) is an unverified vendor-based estimate.
Coding notes: [E224] Credential access means the theft of connection keys and password hashes from the vendor database. The backdoors skip 2FA and Wordfence login protection through auth cookies and hide plugins and accounts, but no security setting was changed, so those columns are NR. No exfiltration from customer sites is documented. The 400k figure is potential exposure only. No Wordfence or Sucuri advisory was retrieved.
People or orgs exposed: NR (TeamUpdraft customer database with names, emails, billing addresses, order history, password hashes, 2FA settings and connection keys believed accessed; no count given as of 29 Oct 2026 update)

Incident: Virtualizor (Softaculous) update channel hijacked via BGP route hijack to deliver malicious update package to hosting providers' Virtualizor servers
Access path: AS62390 (NexonHost) announced a more-specific, RPKI-valid route for Hetzner prefix 162.55.80.0/24 via AS6204 between 28 Aug 20:57 UTC and 30 Aug 06:10 UTC 2026. It diverted Softaculous update and client/billing traffic to an attacker server holding a valid TLS certificate. Update clients did not cryptographically verify packages, so a malicious Virtualizor update installed.
Orgs reached (as reported): Softaculous: malicious update delivered to 'a small number of installations' / 'a handful of servers' that updated during the hijack window; vendor says it 'cannot produce a definitive list of affected servers' (no logs of redirected requests). Provider count not reported.
Coding notes: [E230] Payload function undisclosed. Only IOC is systemd unit java-jre-update.service (Services/tasks Y). SSH-key, account and cron audits are precautionary advice, not observed behaviour. Client-area logins and payment entries may have been diverted, but no credential capture was confirmed. No downstream customer-VPS impact reported. Reach is 'handful', with no exact count. News reports put the hijack at about 33 hours.

Incident: OVHcloud CLI (ovh/ovhcloud-cli) GitHub release binaries v0.11.0–v0.15.0 replaced with GlassWorm-linked secret stealer via compromised developer account
Access path: Developer's personal machine compromised around Oct 2025 via malicious VS Code-type extension (color-picker-universal 2.8.91, GlassWorm); stolen GitHub keys used on 19 Oct 2026 to replace existing release assets (5 releases, 5 platforms + checksums) via Releases API; release immutability disabled; CI/CD and source not affected
Orgs reached (as reported): ~250 downloads during 1h33 window (OVHcloud GHSA-862f-55f5-vmvw); number of organisations not reported; one customer reported it via a GitHub issue (OpenSourceMalware: downstream CI job failed on hash pin)
Coding notes: [E231] Kept 'Vendor or developer account': assets were swapped with a stolen developer account and locally built binaries, bypassing CI, so 'Build or release pipeline' does not fit. The ~250 figure counts downloads, not organisations. No victims or data theft were confirmed, so Data exposed is NR. The stealer collected cloud, SSH, Kubernetes, IDE and AI-tool secrets into an archive and sent it to 45.32.148.174/upload. Behaviours (credential access, archive, exfiltration) set NR at merge: stealer design only, no victim observed (decision 15). Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Incident: HIQ (Boston-area managed IT provider) Quest KACE SMA compromise; attacker's open directory exposed a dump of HIQ's KACE database covering 60+ client organisations
Access path: Internet-facing Quest KACE Systems Management Appliance run by the MSP. Entry via CVE-2025-32975 (authentication bypass, CVSS 10) is inferred from timing, not confirmed. The attacker dumped the appliance's MariaDB database to their own server.
Orgs reached (as reported): 1 MSP (HIQ). KACE database dump held data on over 60 named client organisations in law enforcement, government, education, healthcare and private sector (Hunt.io, 12 May 2026). Access to client systems not shown.
Coding notes: [E257] Hunt.io found the toolkit (reverse shell, SMB sprayer, AddUser.ps1, tunnels) but did not show it used. Entry via CVE-2025-32975 is inferred. KEV added 2026-04-20. No HIQ or regulator notice found. Kept RMM boundary because the KACE platform itself was breached. Only customer data was shown taken, so Service provider holding customer data also fits. Crossed boundary set Y at merge (60+ clients' data exposed).
People or orgs exposed: 60+ client organisations (Hunt.io, 12 May 2026); 21 KACE user accounts with SHA-1 hashes, device inventory, helpdesk tickets

Incident: SK shieldus employee email compromise and leak of client-company documents to dark web (Black Shrantac claim)
Access path: Hacker took over an SK shieldus employee's personal email account (reportedly logged in on a honeypot system). MSIT reportedly found two employees' accounts affected. Work documents in the mailbox, including client-company files and contact details, were taken and posted on the dark web.
Orgs reached (as reported): PIPC: data of SK shieldus and its client companies' staff, number not given. MSIT data given to Rep. Choi Su-jin (news only, Byline Network 27 Oct 2025): about 120 private companies, 15 of them financial firms, plus several public agencies.
Coding notes: [E143] Only the PIPC release (23 Oct 2025) was checked as a primary source. The 120-client and 15.1GB figures (hacker claimed 24GB) come from MSIT data reported by news; with them the band would be Hundreds or more. SK shieldus first said only a honeypot was hit. No PIPC decision found. Relevance changed to MSP-specific: an MSSP's client security documents leaked. Crossed boundary set Y at merge (client data exposed).
People or orgs exposed: NR from primary sources. News: about 120 client companies plus public agencies (MSIT data, Oct 2025).

Access path: Attacker breached the vendor's website (accesspressthemes.com) and injected a dropper into theme and plugin downloads. The dropper installed a cookie-triggered webshell in wp-includes/vars.php on the sites that installed them. Copies from WordPress.org were not affected.
Orgs reached (as reported): Unknown number of compromised websites (Sucuri, Jan 2022). 40 themes and 53 plugins backdoored (Jetpack).
Coding notes: [E079] Year changed from 2021 to 2022: the breach was in September 2021 but first disclosed 18 Jan 2022. Jetpack says the backdoor gave 'full access' to sites. Sucuri saw spam SEO and redirects on infected sites. No count of affected sites. How the vendor site was breached is unknown.

Access path: Attackers breached MonPass's public web server, which held eight webshells or backdoors, and replaced the client installer download with a trojanized one. The installer fetched a BMP image that hid a Cobalt Strike beacon, while also running the real installer.
Orgs reached (as reported): No count published. Avast found it in a customer's environment. MonPass told Avast it had notified affected customers (Avast, July 2021).
Coding notes: [E097] The Cobalt Strike beacon could execute commands, but no post-exploitation activity was reported, so Execute commands is NR. The trust boundary is really a compromised download server rather than an auto-update channel; kept the pre-assigned value. Avast made no attribution. 'More than one' rests on MonPass notifying affected customers (plural).

Access path: The maintainer's npm account was hijacked and used to publish trojanized ua-parser-js versions 0.7.29, 0.8.0 and 1.0.0. These pulled down a cryptominer (and, on Windows, a credential stealer) at install time.
Orgs reached (as reported): No confirmed organisation count. The package had about 6-7 million weekly downloads (news and Rapid7, Oct 2021); downloads are not organisations.
Coding notes: [E100] Counted as a maintainer-account takeover. The miner and stealer payload is described by vendors (Rapid7, Fortinet) from malware analysis, so Credential access is NR under the design-inference rule. Primary advisories describe no confirmed victim organisations. The maintainer's account-hijack statement is in GitHub issue #536, which timed out when fetched.

Access path: Compromised npm maintainer account. On 4 Nov 2021 it was used to publish malicious coa (2.0.3, 2.0.4, 2.1.1, 2.1.3, 3.1.3) and rc (1.2.9, 1.3.9, 2.3.9) versions. A preinstall script ran compile.js, which started compile.bat. The batch file downloaded sdd.dll and ran it with regsvr32.
Orgs reached (as reported): No downstream organisations confirmed. The two packages had about 23M weekly downloads combined (news). Press reported broken React build pipelines worldwide, but named no organisations.
Coding notes: [E101] Account takeover is per npm's statement as quoted in news; the advisories do not name the vector. CERT-EU's password-stealing, keylogging and screenshot functions come from payload analysis, so Credential access is NR. Payload descriptions conflict (Qakbot, DanaBot, cryptominer). Pipeline breakage is reported in news only.

Access path: Exploited zero-days in the legacy Accellion File Transfer Appliance: one patched in Dec 2020, then CVE-2021-27101 SQL injection, CVE-2021-27102/27104 OS command execution and CVE-2021-27103 SSRF. Attackers deployed a webshell (DEWMODE per Mandiant), downloaded hosted files and cleaned logs. UNC2546 did the exploitation; UNC2582/Clop did the extortion.
Orgs reached (as reported): Accellion: fewer than 100 of about 300 FTA customers were victims, fewer than 25 with significant data theft. CISA lists victims in AU, NZ, SG, the UK and the US across government, medical, legal, telecom, finance and energy, with no total.
Coding notes: [E120] FTA was mostly customer-run, so the trust boundary is arguably vendor product rather than a provider holding data; kept the pre-assigned value to match E033. Accellion's early figure was 'less than 50', later 'fewer than 100'. CISA says the W1 token 'may' have been exposed, so credentials are NR. Extortion, not encryption. Health Net (HHS) is merged here. The Kiteworks and Mandiant pages were seen through search only, not fetched. Tier 3->2 after tier re-check (2026-11-26): customer-run appliances exploited and a web shell installed; no supplier delivery channel and no account creation, so decision 17 does not apply.
People or orgs exposed: Fewer than 100 customer organisations (Accellion, Feb 2021); individuals total NR

Access path: Ransomware attack on 1 Dec 2021 on a Battelle for Kids server that stored district student and staff data (course history, performance-task scores for teacher evaluations). Initial access vector not reported.
Orgs reached (as reported): Chicago Public Schools (CPS notice). News also names Ohio districts: Upper Arlington, Fairfield, Lakota and Valley View. BFK said it notified 'all impacted school systems' but gave no number. The Journal put the total at 600K+ students.
Coding notes: [E121] Year changed from 2021 to 2022: the attack was in Dec 2021, but the first public disclosure (Ohio districts, then CPS) came in Apr-May 2022. The only primary source is the customer's (CPS) notice. The Ohio districts and BFK's statement come from news. Tier 2 follows the shared-infrastructure ransomware convention. No group claimed it.
People or orgs exposed: 495,448 students and 56,138 staff at CPS (CPS notice, May 2022); total across districts NR (news: 600K+ students)

Access path: NR (initial access not disclosed). Unauthorised access to and acquisition of CaptureRx (NEC Networks LLC) electronic files on 6 Feb 2021, confirmed 19 Feb 2021. The files held patient data for its 340B healthcare-provider clients.
Orgs reached (as reported): Multiple covered entities filed their own notices and HHS reports, including Southwest Virginia CHS, Gifford, UPMC, Bayhealth, Walmart, Ascension and MetroHealth. Reported counts vary over time: 17, about 130 and 200+ organisations (news). No primary total.
Coding notes: [E122] CaptureRx never called it ransomware; covered entities and media did, so Ransomware is NR. The Maine AG page returned 403, so the 2,420,141 figure was seen in search results only. HHS lists 1,656,569 under NEC Networks; some clients reported separately. 'Dozens' is a lower bound.

Access path: Attacker breached SITA Passenger Service System (US) servers in Atlanta, which hold airline passenger and frequent-flyer data. Technique not disclosed.
Orgs reached (as reported): About a dozen airlines named in airline disclosures reported by news (Air India, Singapore Airlines, Finnair, British Airways, Lufthansa, Malaysia Airlines and others). SITA gave no count.
Coding notes: [E203] Airline statements were seen only through news. Singapore Airlines and Air India said passwords were not involved; left Access credentials NR because those statements were not read directly. Reach band Dozens is borderline (about 10+ airlines confirmed). SITA is arguably an airline IT outsourcer but PSS is hosted SaaS, so kept General.
People or orgs exposed: About 4.5 million Air India passengers (Air India, May 2021) plus about 580,000 Singapore Airlines members (Mar 2021), both via news

Access path: Attacker gained 'full access' to ECL's AWS-hosted myCare Integrity EMR. It ran 'discover' and 'delete' commands, deleting databases and system configuration files that held multiple practices' PHI.
Orgs reached (as reported): Dozens of ophthalmology practices filed notices (for example Spectrum Eye Physicians and Wolfe Clinic, 542,776 patients). Industry tallies (TechTarget) exceed 2 million patients.
Coding notes: [E209] Year changed from 2021 to 2022: the attack was 4 Dec 2021 but first disclosure was ECL's notice of 1 Mar 2022. Notices call it 'ransomware' but describe only deletion, no encryption, so ransomware is NR. ECL found no evidence PHI was taken but cannot rule it out. Backups were used to restore data, not altered. ECL's own notice was not found.
People or orgs exposed: Over 2 million patients across dozens of practices (TechTarget tally, 2022, secondary). Wolfe Clinic: 542,776 (2022).

Access path: Unauthorized access to Elekta's first-generation cloud-based storage system (2-20 Apr 2021). Attacker acquired a copy of the database holding oncology patient data for multiple provider customers.
Orgs reached (as reported): About 42 health systems had data affected (Elekta spokesperson via press). About 170 US customers had service disrupted (Elekta). Named victims include Northwestern Memorial, Renown, Yale New Haven, Lifespan, Southcoast, McLaren, Jefferson.
Coding notes: [E213] Primary sources exist (Elekta statement, provider notices, HHS OCR filings) but I only saw them quoted in HIPAA Journal. Verify before counting. Ransomware was suspected and never confirmed by Elekta, so the incident name may overstate it. Elekta first said no data was extracted, then confirmed the database copy. At merge: HHS OCR row for Northwestern Memorial names Elekta (primary); multi-customer count from Elekta statement via press.
People or orgs exposed: No total reported. Northwestern Memorial 201,197; Renown 65,181; McLaren about 64,000 (2021 notices, via press)

Incident: Heroku and Travis CI OAuth token theft
Access path: Compromised Heroku machine-account token gave access to Heroku databases. Attacker downloaded customers' stored GitHub integration OAuth tokens and used them, with Travis CI tokens, to list and clone private repos. An AWS key found in npm repos gave access to npm infrastructure.
Orgs reached (as reported): 'Dozens' of organizations including npm (GitHub). Heroku says 'a small number' of its customers had repos cloned; Heroku customer password hashes were exfiltrated.
Coding notes: [E050] MSP-specific because customers were reached through a cloud hosting/PaaS provider (Heroku). This is borderline; General is also defensible. Deploy software = N because GitHub says no npm packages were modified. Travis CI says its key gave no customer data access. Service disruption = Heroku revoking tokens and disabling its GitHub integration.

Access path: Attacker placed a backdoored Electron installer (malicious main.js), signed with Comm100's valid certificate, on Comm100's download site. It fetched a second-stage script that gave a cmd.exe remote shell, then dropped a DLL loader via mdmerge.exe sideloading.
Orgs reached (as reported): Organizations in industrial, healthcare, technology, manufacturing, insurance and telecom sectors in North America and Europe (CrowdStrike, no count). Reuters cited about a dozen victims (unconfirmed).
Coding notes: [E051] Read data = host information collection. Deploy software is based on CrowdStrike's described 'likely follow-on' installation of a loader DLL and in-memory payload. Trust boundary could also be Build or release pipeline; how the signed build was compromised was not reported. China nexus (moderate confidence).

Incident: Agrius 'Fantasy' wiper delivered via Israeli diamond-industry software developer's update mechanism
Access path: Developer's software suite / update mechanism abused (ESET assessment: all victims were customers, the wiper filename mimicked legitimate versions, and it ran from the temp directory at the software's check-in time); clean updates were pushed within hours
Orgs reached (as reported): At least 5 customer organisations in South Africa, Israel (IT support firm, diamond wholesaler, HR consultancy) and Hong Kong (jeweller) (ESET, 7 Dec 2022)
Coding notes: [E077] The update vector is ESET's assessment and the developer did not respond, so the developer is unnamed. MiniDump/SecretsDump appeared at the South African victim in Feb 2022, before the wiper, and that access path may differ from the update path. Sandals moved laterally with PsExec over SMB. Wiping also cleared event logs and the MBR. Wiper, not ransomware.

Access path: Legitimate maintainer published sabotaged versions to npm: colors 1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.44-liberty-2 (infinite loop printing 'LIBERTY' junk) and faker 6.6.6 (functional code removed)
Orgs reached (as reported): Downstream organisations not counted; colors had about 20M weekly downloads and faker about 2.8M (Snyk/news). Clever Cloud told users of its npm CLI to upgrade as a precaution
Coding notes: [E102] Impact was denial of service only (CVE-2021-23567, GHSA-gh88-3pxp-6fm8), so tier is NR under the 'none reported' rule. Read data and credentials are coded N because the advisories describe only a loop or removed code. News widely cites AWS CDK breakage, but I could not confirm it from a primary source. Download counts are not organisations. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Legitimate maintainer published node-ipc 10.1.1/10.1.2 with a geolocation-triggered file-overwrite payload (Russia/Belarus), and 9.2.2/11.0.0 adding the peacenotwar dependency that drops a desktop text file
Orgs reached (as reported): Vue.js CLI (@vue/cli 9.x range) and Unity (Unity Hub bundled node-ipc 9.2.2; hotfix 3.1.1 on 16 Mar 2022) per Snyk; node-ipc had about 1.06M weekly downloads
Coding notes: [E103] The confirmed downstream products (Vue CLI, Unity Hub) got the 9.2.2 peacenotwar variant, which only drops a file. I found no primary confirmation of actual file wiping at a named organisation. Execute Y because the package code ran on hosts and overwrote files when geo-triggered. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Incident: ctx PyPI package takeover via expired maintainer domain
Access path: Expired maintainer email domain re-registered on 14 May 2022, then a PyPI password reset gave account takeover. Original releases were deleted and replaced with malicious copies until mitigation on 24 May 2022
Orgs reached (as reported): Organisations not counted; about 27,000 malicious downloads (PyPI admins via The Register). PSF: anyone installing ctx between 14 and 24 May 2022 was impacted
Coding notes: [E104] Trust boundary changed from 'Plugin, extension or package' to 'Vendor or developer account' because the root cause was maintainer-account takeover; revert if the study keeps package incidents uniform. The payload sent environment variables (incl. AWS keys) to a Heroku endpoint (SANS ISC). The self-described researcher hit phpass the same way. The download figure comes from news citing PyPI. Boundary kept as Plugin, extension or package at merge for consistency with other maintainer-account takeovers. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Incident: MiMi chat app installer trojanized (Iron Tiger / APT27)
Access path: Attacker controlled the server hosting the legitimate (unsigned) MiMi installers from at least Nov 2021 and inserted packed loader code into electron-main.js of new releases (Windows 2.2.0, macOS 2.3.0 in May 2022)
Orgs reached (as reported): 13 targets (5 HyperBro, 8 rshell) in Taiwan and the Philippines. One victim identified, a Taiwanese gaming developer; a Taiwanese IT developer was suspected (Trend Micro, 12 Aug 2022)
Coding notes: [E106] This was a distribution-server compromise rather than an auto-update channel, so 'Build or release pipeline' could also fit. Targets are machines, not confirmed organisations: one organisation is confirmed, so the band is Unknown (more than one). rshell's shell and file commands come from malware design, so the behaviours are NR. SEKOIA reported the campaign in parallel.

Access path: Phished PyPI maintainer credentials used to publish malicious releases of legitimate packages (exotel 0.1.6; spam 2.0.2, 4.0.2)
Orgs reached (as reported): No downstream organisations confirmed; exotel had 480,000+ total downloads and spam 200,000+ (Checkmarx)
Coding notes: [E107] Malicious releases downloaded and ran python-install.scr, the JuiceStealer infostealer. Its credential theft comes from malware analysis, so behaviours are NR. Capability is coded from what the distributed code did. Some reports also name deep-translator. SentinelLabs report not fetched (HTTP 429). PyPI tweet seen only as cited by Checkmarx.

Access path: Intrusion into FishPig license/distribution system; malicious code injected into Helper/License.php of paid Magento 2 extensions, which fetched and ran a Linux binary
Orgs reached (as reported): Not counted; FishPig says assume all paid Magento 2 modules were infected; free packages have 200,000+ downloads but were unaffected (Sansec)
Coding notes: [E108] Injected PHP used system commands to download lic.bin (Rekoobe), which runs in memory and waits for commands. Sansec saw no follow-on C2 abuse. The rogue 'rangex' admin account appears only in a vendor blurb, so it is NR. Earliest infection: FishPig says 6 Aug, Sansec says by 19 Aug. Count of infected stores not reported.

Access path: Compromised dYdX npm publishing account used to push minor-version releases with malicious preinstall hook (@dydxprotocol/solo, perpetual, node-service-base-dev)
Orgs reached (as reported): No affected organisations confirmed; 120,000+ combined downloads (Mend); used by at least 44 crypto projects (BleepingComputer, news)
Coding notes: [E109] Capability is from Mend's payload analysis: it downloaded setup.py and stole SSH keys, AWS credentials and environment variables. No victims were observed, so behaviours are NR. Mend could not confirm how the account was compromised; the staff-account claim comes from BleepingComputer citing dYdX. Not the separate Feb 2026 dYdX v4 incident.

Access path: Unauthorized access to MCG systems holding customers' patient data (vector not disclosed)
Orgs reached (as reported): At least 8 provider customers issued their own notices (e.g., Phelps Health, Avera, IU Health, CHI Health; TechTarget list); MCG also notified for the customers listed in its Maine AG Exhibit A
Coding notes: [E124] MCG says the party 'previously obtained' the data, so Exfiltration is Y. Counts conflict: about 1.1M people in the Maine AG filing, 793,283 on HHS OCR (some customers filed separately). Exhibit A could hold more customers, which could make the band Dozens. The ransom demand is from news and the lawsuit only, so NR. Maine AG and MCG press-release pages returned 403.
People or orgs exposed: About 1,100,000 individuals (MCG filing to Maine AG, June 2022); 793,283 on HHS OCR

Access path: Unauthorized access to ILS network holding health-plan clients' member data (vector not disclosed)
Orgs reached (as reported): Several health plans (VNS Health notice); named: Florida Community Care, Florida Complete Care (ILS subsidiaries), VNS Health; other clients unnamed
Coding notes: [E175] Preliminary website notice 2 Sep 2022 (Year 2022); letters mailed from 14 Mar 2023. The 4,226,508 figure is from the Maine AG filing as reported by press. Press says systems became inaccessible, but that is not confirmed in a primary source I could read, so Service disruption is NR. The CA AG PDF text could not be extracted.
People or orgs exposed: Up to 4,226,508 individuals (ILS filing to Maine AG, Mar 2023)

Access path: Ransomware on the vendor's own systems, which held member mailing data files for many client health plans
Orgs reached (as reported): 34 health insurers/providers listed in OTP's notice; others reached through subcontractor Matrix Medical Network (news reports 37 in total)
Coding notes: [E212] OTP found encrypted files on 28 Apr 2022; intrusion window 27 Apr to 3 Jun 2022. Notices say an actor 'may have accessed' data files, so Read data is NR. Data exposed is coded Y because individuals were notified. No ransomware group named. Clients' own systems were unaffected. Maine AG and HHS pages could not be fetched (403); the Maine figure comes from search snippets.

Access path: Malware on an engineer's laptop stole a 2FA-backed SSO session cookie. The attacker used it to reach production, generate tokens and exfiltrate customer secrets, and pulled the encryption keys from a running process.
Orgs reached (as reported): Fewer than 5 customers reported unauthorized access to third-party systems (CircleCI, Jan 2023); all customers told to rotate secrets
Coding notes: [E029] Lateral movement is coded Y for the stolen session cookie (T1550.004) used to escalate into production. The total number of customers whose secrets were exfiltrated was not reported. Reach counts only customers confirming downstream misuse. The first customer token compromise was flagged 29 Dec 2022 and disclosure came 4 Jan 2023.

Access path: Cl0p exploited a SQL injection in internet-facing MOVEit Transfer and installed the LEMURLOOT web shell. It enumerated the database, took Azure storage keys, created admin accounts and exfiltrated files. These included files that service providers such as Maximus, IBM and Welltok held for many clients.
Orgs reached (as reported): Emsisoft (not primary) counts about 2,700+ organisations and 93M+ records. Maximus 8-K: 8 to 11 million individuals across government customers. CISA gives no MOVEit victim count.
Coding notes: [E033] Recommend one incident; HHS business associates (IBM, Maximus, Welltok, TMG, WPS) are victims of the same campaign, not separate incidents. Some victims, such as IBM for its government clients, were reached through an IT outsourcer, which partly fits MSP-specific; kept General. CISA does not report encryption. Software deployment and Create/modify accounts are coded Y for the web-shell install and 'Health Check Service' admin accounts.
People or orgs exposed: 8 to 11 million individuals (Maximus 8-K, Jul 2023); about 93M records industry-wide (Emsisoft, non-primary)

Access path: An SMS phishing message and a deepfake voice call got an employee's credentials and MFA codes. The attacker registered a device in Okta and used the employee's cloud-synced Google Authenticator codes to reach the VPN and internal admin tools. From there the attacker took over customer accounts.
Orgs reached (as reported): 27 cloud customers, all in crypto (Retool, Sep 2023)
Coding notes: [E073] Account takeover by changing emails and resetting passwords gives Create/modify accounts and tier 3. Read data is Y because the attacker 'looked around some Retool apps'. The $15M Fortress Trust crypto theft is reported only in news. Retool says on-prem and managed accounts were explicitly unaffected.

Incident: Evasive Panda MgBot update hijack (Tencent QQ)
Access path: Legitimate QQ updater (QQUrlMgr.exe) and other QQ components downloaded and ran the MgBot installer over the unencrypted HTTP update channel. The cause is either a compromise of QQ's update servers or interception in transit (ISP or router); ESET considers the two equally unproven
Orgs reached (as reported): ESET: targets in Gansu, Guangdong and Jiangsu (China), most of them members of one international NGO, plus one victim in Nigeria. No total count given
Coding notes: [E112] Activity ran 2020-2021 and was found in Jan 2022; first public disclosure was Apr 2023. ESET cannot say whether this was a supplier compromise or interception (AitM). MgBot plugin capabilities (credential theft, keylogging, file theft) come from malware analysis, not from observed victim activity, so they are coded NR. Victims are individuals, so the organisation count is unclear.

Incident: Ghostly S3 bucket takeover of npm binary (bignum)
Access path: The attacker re-registered the abandoned AWS S3 bucket that bignum's install script pulled prebuilt binaries from. The trojanised binary was then served during npm install
Orgs reached (as reported): None confirmed. Checkmarx reports no victim or download counts
Coding notes: [E116] Checkmarx's analysis of the binary shows theft of user ID, passwords, environment variables and hostname, sent out in the user-agent of a request to the bucket. That comes from malware design, not from confirmed victims, so it is coded NR. Software deployment is Y because the binary was being served live. A borderline include, since no victim is confirmed.

Access path: Unauthorized access to PJ&A's own network (method not reported). Customer patient data held there was accessed between 7 and 19 Apr 2023
Orgs reached (as reported): PJ&A: 'multiple covered entities'. Named customers include Northwell Health (about 3.9M), Cook County Health (about 1.2M), North Kansas City Hospital and The South Bend Clinic
Coding notes: [E156] PJ&A's notice template (filed with California AG, 3 Nov 2023) says a database 'was obtained', so Exfiltration is Y. Four customers are confirmed by name; the full customer count is not published and may be higher. Access method not disclosed. The HHS OCR figure was not fetched directly; it is cited via BleepingComputer.

Access path: Unknown actor accessed HealthEC systems from 14 to 23 Jul 2023 (method not reported) and copied files containing client patient data
Orgs reached (as reported): 17 client organisations (HealthEC notice, Dec 2023), including Corewell Health, HonorHealth, Beaumont ACO, TennCare, UMC Princeton Physicians' Organization and Alliance for Integrated Care of New York
Coding notes: [E157] The state AG, TennCare and HHS pages blocked automated fetching. Their facts (files copied, 17 clients, 4,452,782 people) are taken from news reports of those notices (BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek). healthec.com/cyber-incident now redirects to elliginthealth.com. Investigation concluded 24 Oct 2023.

Incident: ESO Solutions ransomware (EMS/hospital software provider, detected 28 Sep 2023); patient data of multiple hospital-system customers accessed
Access path: An unauthorised third party accessed and encrypted some of ESO's own computer systems (detected and stopped 28 Sep 2023; the Maine filing gives 17 Sep as the breach date). Forensics found that the affected parts of the network held hospital customers' patient PI/PHI. ESO restored from backups. No intrusion into customer systems: TMH says its own systems were not affected.
Orgs reached (as reported): No official customer count. HIPAA Journal (news, from ESO's notice) names about 12 health systems and more than 20 hospitals, e.g. Ascension, Baptist Memorial, CaroMont, CHS, Forrest Health, HCA, Memorial Gulfport, Providence, TMH, UHS/Valley Health. TMH confirms 9,566 of its patients (TMH notice, Dec 2023).
Coding notes: [E158] Execute commands Y and tier 2 follow the hosting-ransomware convention. The Dozens band counts hospitals named in news drawn from ESO's notice and is unconfirmed; it could be Several if counted by health system. ESO says data 'may have been acquired', so Exfiltration is NR. The Maine and Vermont PDFs returned 403, so the 2.7M figure comes from the Maine listing and news. No ransomware group was named.
People or orgs exposed: 2.7 million individuals (ESO notification to Maine AG, Dec 2023)

Incident: Fortra GoAnywhere MFT / MFTaaS zero-day campaign (CVE-2023-0669, Cl0p claimed), Jan-Feb 2023
Access path: A pre-auth deserialisation zero-day (CVE-2023-0669) in GoAnywhere MFT was used from 18 Jan 2023 (on-prem) and 28-30 Jan in Fortra-hosted MFTaaS. The attacker created unauthorised user accounts in some MFTaaS customer environments and used them to download files. In some environments it also installed Netcat and Errors.jsp. Fortra neutralised MFTaaS activity on 31 Jan and reprovisioned a clean environment.
Orgs reached (as reported): Fortra: 'some MFTaaS customer environments' (no count). CHS 8-K (13 Feb 2023): Fortra breach exposed data of about 1M CHS-affiliate patients. Cl0p claimed about 130 organisations (news, unconfirmed).
Coding notes: [E221] The Fortra summary page (17 Apr 2023) is behind a bot wall, so details come from its text quoted in search and news; the CHS 8-K was seen only as a search excerpt. Counts because Fortra's own hosted MFTaaS tenants were breached. Other victims (NationsBenefits, Rubrik, Hatch Bank) were not checked against primary sources. Cl0p attribution is from news only.
People or orgs exposed: About 1 million individuals for CHS alone (CHS 8-K, 13 Feb 2023); campaign total not reported

Incident: XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) in liblzma 5.6.0/5.6.1 release tarballs, inserted by a long-term co-maintainer
Access path: Over about two years, 'Jia Tan' gained co-maintainer and release rights, then shipped release tarballs with obfuscated build-script and test-file changes. These injected a backdoor into liblzma that hooks sshd's RSA authentication (via systemd linkage) and lets the holder of the attacker's key run code before authentication. Andres Freund found it on 29 Mar 2024, before it reached stable distribution releases.
Orgs reached (as reported): Shipped in development or rolling distributions: Fedora 41/Rawhide (Red Hat), Debian unstable/testing, openSUSE Tumbleweed/MicroOS, Kali, Arch (not exploitable). No confirmed exploitation of any organisation.
Coding notes: [E035] Execute commands Y reflects the backdoor's reported RCE capability; no use was observed, so behaviours are NR (design only). The Several band counts distributions that shipped it, not victim organisations; it could be Unknown (more than one). Only the CISA page was fetched; the Red Hat and Openwall URLs are standard references and were not fetched. The trust boundary could arguably be 'Vendor or developer account'. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Incident: Ultralytics YOLO PyPI package compromise via GitHub Actions (versions 8.3.41, 8.3.42, 8.3.45, 8.3.46 with XMRig cryptominer), Dec 2024
Access path: The attacker exploited a known GitHub Actions script injection through crafted pull requests (#18018, #18020) and poisoned the Actions cache used in the build. The project's normal release workflow then published 8.3.41/8.3.42 with miner code. A second wave (8.3.45/8.3.46) used an unrevoked PyPI API token available to the workflow. PyPI removed the versions.
Orgs reached (as reported): Number of downstream organisations not reported. Users reported the miner running after install (news and threat-intel reports); download counts were not verified.
Coding notes: [E084] Execute commands Y because the miner ran on install, per reports. Behaviours are left NR because the miner download comes from payload analysis (ReversingLabs, Wiz), not a victim investigation. Users' reports of miner activity could support Software deployment Y. The Ultralytics GitHub issue was not fetched. Download counts were not verified, and no organisations are confirmed. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Stolen npm publish token of a team member (maintainer statement); how it was stolen is not reported
Orgs reached (as reported): Not reported; malicious v1.1.7 was live about 1 hour from 02:01 UTC on 19 Dec 2024 (Rspack release notes). No downstream organisations confirmed
Coding notes: [E086] Execute commands=Y because the maintainers say the malicious code ran via the postinstall script. The XMRig miner and credential collection come only from Socket/Sonatype malware analysis, so they are coded NR under the malware-design convention. The same token theft also hit the Vant package, which could be a related event. No affected organisations were confirmed. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Compromised publish-access npm account (advisory). Anza's root-cause analysis, as reported by news, says it was a spear-phishing npm org invite
Orgs reached (as reported): Not reported. Projects that updated between 15:20 and 20:25 UTC on 3 Dec 2024 may be affected (advisory). News citing Solscan reports about $130k-$160k stolen. Package has about 50M total downloads (ReversingLabs)
Coding notes: [E089] The advisory says the malware exfiltrates private key material, and real theft followed (news/Solscan), so Credential access and Exfiltration are Y. The advisory names bots and other projects handling private keys as affected but gives no organisation count. Dollar figures come from news only. I did not fetch Anza's postmortem directly. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Employee npm account taken over via phishing (LottieFiles). Versions were published directly to npm, bypassing GitHub and the normal release process
Orgs reached (as reported): LottieFiles reports only a 'limited set of users', mainly sites that pulled the latest version from public CDNs. No organisation count
Coding notes: [E092] The drainer showed site visitors a 'Connect Wallet' prompt, which is similar to Polyfill: it harms visitors and gives no admin capability, so the tier is NR. LottieFiles says no customer data, services or workspaces were affected. News reports of one large BTC loss are unconfirmed by a primary source. Accounts differ on whether access came from phishing or a CI automation token. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: NR
Orgs reached (as reported): At least 3 named customers disrupted: Starbucks, Morrisons, Sainsbury's (customer statements via news). Blue Yonder has 3,000+ customers and gave no count
Coding notes: [E130] Tier 2 under the provider-ransomware convention. Termite claimed 680GB stolen; Blue Yonder acknowledged the claim but did not confirm it, so Exfiltration and Data exposed are NR. The customer-update page now returns 404 and its content was seen only through search snippets. Borderline MSP-specific because a hosted environment was hit, but Blue Yonder is a SaaS application vendor, not an IT provider, so General.

Access path: NR
Orgs reached (as reported): About 46 client organisations (45 listed on the Kelly website per news), including CareFirst, Guardian and Beam Benefits
Coding notes: [E132] Year changed from the pre-assigned 2024 to 2025: the intrusion was in Dec 2024 but first public notice came in 2025 (about 264k reported in April, later raised). Both primary URLs returned 403 to me, so the figures come from SecurityWeek/SecurityAffairs reports of the Maine AG filings. No ransomware group claimed it. The client-org count is from news.
People or orgs exposed: 553,660 individuals (Maine AG filing, as reported July 2025)

Access path: Unauthorised access to IMS systems from 29 Oct 2023; certain systems encrypted 2 Nov 2023; client policyholder data held by IMS exposed
Orgs reached (as reported): Multiple IMS clients named in state filings (Bank of America 57,028 customers; T. Rowe Price RPS; Nassau Life; others). Total 6,078,263 individuals per IMS Maine AG filing, 27 Jun 2024
Coding notes: [E189] First disclosed Nov 2023 (Infosys 6-K), so Year is 2023, not the pre-assigned 2024. Maine/CA AG pages returned 403 and the PDF did not extract; figures come from search snippets of those filings. LockBit claim is from news only. Exfiltration NR because acquisition wording was not verified. Reach band: Several confirmed clients, possibly Dozens. IMS is a BPO outsourcer but not IT management, so General.

Access path: Third party gained unauthorised access to CDK systems (discovered 19 Jun 2024; second incident 20 Jun); CDK shut down its hosted dealer management system, used by dealer customers
Orgs reached (as reported): About 15,000 dealer locations disrupted (CDK customer base, per news). Six listed dealer groups filed 8-Ks (Lithia, AutoNation, Group 1, Penske, Sonic, Asbury). Maine AG notice: 36 individuals (CDK vendors)
Coding notes: [E200] BlackSuit ransomware attribution and the reported ransom come from news only; CDK did not confirm, so Ransomware is NR and tier is 1 rather than the shared-infrastructure default of 2. Exfiltration Y because the state notice says the third party obtained a copy of files (CDK vendor data, 36 people). Dealer consumer data exposure was never established. The 15,000 figure is CDK's customer base. AG pages returned 403; content is from snippets.
People or orgs exposed: 36 individuals (CDK vendors; Maine AG filing, Sep 2024)

Access path: Compromised credentials used on a Change Healthcare Citrix remote-access portal without MFA (12 Feb 2024); lateral movement, exfiltration, ransomware deployed 21 Feb 2024
Orgs reached (as reported): Thousands of providers, pharmacies and payers disrupted; PHI of many covered entities' patients (UHG / HHS OCR)
Coding notes: [E211] Credential access Y means stolen credentials were used for initial access, not observed dumping. The testimony PDF was not opened directly; its content is from search snippets. ALPHV/BlackCat attribution and the $22M ransom were acknowledged by UHG. The count rose from 100M to 190M to 192.7M (final).
People or orgs exposed: 192.7 million individuals (UHG final figure on HHS OCR breach portal, Jul-Aug 2025)

Access path: Stolen OAuth refresh/access tokens of Gainsight-published Salesforce connected apps (285 tokens; about 250 validated 22 Oct 2025) used to call Salesforce APIs against customer orgs, 16-19 Nov 2025
Orgs reached (as reported): 'Only a handful of customers' had data affected (Gainsight). Google GTIG reported 200+ potentially affected instances. Attackers claimed about 760, unverified
Coding notes: [E032] Mandiant could not find the token source and found no evidence of compromise of Gainsight systems; tokens dated 2017-Aug 2023. Possibly linked to the Salesloft Drift / ShinyHunters campaign. 'Handful' read as Several; GTIG's 200+ is potential, not confirmed. Ransomware N per Gainsight's explicit no-exfiltration-from-its-environment statement is weak; treat as NR if strict.

Access path: Bash injection in a pull_request_target PR-validation workflow let the attacker trigger publish.yml and send the npm token to a webhook. Malicious nx/@nx versions were published on 26 Aug 2025, and the Nx Console VS Code extension auto-installed nx@latest. A postinstall script used local AI CLIs to inventory and steal secrets.
Orgs reached (as reported): Wiz: Phase 2 hit at least 480 compromised accounts (about two-thirds organisations) and made more than 6,700 private repos public. The Wiz post-incident total was 2,180 accounts and 7,200 repos across three phases. Phase 3 hit one organisation (500 repos). GitGuardian counts 10,767 repos made public.
Coding notes: [E037] Root cause was a CI workflow flaw, so 'Build or release pipeline' also fits; kept the pre-assigned boundary. Malware appended 'sudo shutdown -h 0' to shell rc files, treated as command execution. Reach of about 320 organisations is derived from Wiz's two-thirds share. Account and repo counts differ between Wiz and GitGuardian. Ransomware N is inferred: no source reports encryption. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.
People or orgs exposed: At least 480 accounts (about two-thirds organisations), more than 6,700 repos made public (Wiz, Sep 2025). 2,180 accounts and 7,200 repos in total (Wiz post-incident analysis).

Incident: Shai-Hulud 2.0 ('Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming') npm worm
Access path: Maintainer CI secrets were stolen through pull_request_target 'pwn request' workflows (PostHog bot PAT, then npm token). Malicious preinstall versions were published from 24 Nov 2025 (PostHog, Postman, AsyncAPI, Zapier, ENS). The payload installs Bun, runs TruffleHog and republishes the victims' own packages with stolen npm tokens.
Orgs reached (as reported): Zscaler: more than 700 packages, more than 27,000 repos, about 14,000 secrets across 487 organisations. Unit 42: more than 25,000 repos across about 350 users. Wiz: more than 30,000 repos and 'hundreds of companies' with leaked secrets; about 24,000 environment files.
Coding notes: [E040] Kept separate from E039: different wave, payload and entry point; the coordinator may merge. Remote command and Services/tasks come from Unit 42's self-hosted GitHub runner backdoor (commands sent through Discussions). Unit 42 reports a home-directory wipe as fallback. Software deployment means worm republishing packages and installing Bun. The 487-organisation figure is Zscaler's.
People or orgs exposed: About 14,000 secrets across 487 organisations (Zscaler, Nov 2025). More than 30,000 repos (Wiz, 1 Dec 2025).

Access path: Leaked Open VSX developer tokens (the Eclipse Foundation confirms) let attackers push malicious updates to legitimate extensions, e.g. CodeJoy, from 17 Oct 2025. Payload is hidden in invisible Unicode and uses Solana and Google Calendar for C2. Stolen npm, GitHub and OpenVSX credentials let it spread to more extensions. Later waves continued into 2026.
Orgs reached (as reported): Koi: 7 OpenVSX extensions plus 1 VS Code Marketplace extension in the first wave, 35,800 installs (Eclipse says this is inflated by bots). No victim organisations confirmed in the sources checked.
Coding notes: [E041] Koi reports HVNC hidden remote desktop and a SOCKS proxy (Remote command Y), and spread through stolen credentials (Software deployment Y). Eclipse disputes the 'self-propagating worm' framing and the install count. Koi later said it saw a partial victim list on the attacker's server, not verified here. Reach stays Unknown. Later waves (Nov 2025, Jan to Mar 2026) may need separate events.
People or orgs exposed: NR (35,800 installs per Koi, Oct 2025; installs are not organisations)

Incident: TriZetto Provider Solutions client web portal accessed
Access path: An unauthorized actor got into a TPS web portal that provider customers use. From Nov 2024 they accessed insurance-eligibility verification records until detection on 2 Oct 2025. Affected providers were notified from 9 Dec 2025.
Orgs reached (as reported): TPS has not given a client count. HIPAA Journal lists 46 affected providers and covered entities, including through OCHIN, and calls the list not exhaustive.
Coding notes: [E058] The notice says records were 'accessed', not exfiltrated, so Exfiltration is NR. The client count (46 named) is a news compilation of covered-entity notices. Data exposed: names, addresses, DOB, SSNs, insurance and Medicare IDs, with no financial data. Disclosed to providers in Dec 2025 and to individuals in early 2026.
People or orgs exposed: 3,433,965 individuals (Oregon AG filing, 26 Jan 2026 update, via HIPAA Journal). More than 3.6 million across state filings.

Access path: A threat actor was in part of Conduent's network from 21 Oct 2024, detected 13 Jan 2025. It caused operational disruption and exfiltrated files tied to a limited number of clients, including state government programme and health-plan end-users. SafePay claimed it as ransomware.
Orgs reached (as reported): Conduent 8-K: files for 'a limited number of clients'. News names several state agencies (e.g. Wisconsin, Oregon, Texas residents) and corporate clients, but there is no confirmed client count.
Coding notes: [E059] Conduent never confirms ransomware; only SafePay claimed it, so Ransomware is NR and tier is 1. Under the shared-infrastructure ransomware convention, tier would be '2 Endpoint action'. The 25M figure is from Wisconsin's breach page as reported by TechCrunch, not checked directly. Oregon reports 10.5M and Texas 15.4M.
People or orgs exposed: At least 25 million individuals (Wisconsin breach notification page, Feb 2026, per TechCrunch). 10.5 million reported to Oregon (Oct 2025).

Incident: React Native ARIA and gluestack-ui npm compromise
Access path: Leaked npm access token of an authorised maintainer (no 2FA) used to publish malicious versions of 16 @react-native-aria packages and @gluestack-ui/utils on 6-7 June 2025, with an obfuscated RAT in the package code
Orgs reached (as reported): No downstream organisations confirmed. Over 1 million combined weekly downloads (Aikido/gluestack). gluestack reports no confirmed system-level compromises and an exposure window of about 17 hours.
Coding notes: [E091] Execute commands is coded from the RAT capabilities described in the reports (arbitrary shell, file upload). No victim activity was observed, so behaviours are NR. The vendor says impact was minimal and there is no evidence of exfiltration. Aikido links this to the rand-user-agent campaign through a near-identical payload. The vendor lists gluestack-ui/core and Aikido lists gluestack-ui/utils. Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Outdated npm automation token (no 2FA) belonging to the maintainer, WebScrapingAPI, used to publish malicious versions 1.0.110, 2.0.83 and 2.0.84 carrying a RAT. The maintainer says its repo, build pipeline and network were not breached.
Orgs reached (as reported): No downstream organisations confirmed. About 45,000 weekly downloads (Aikido); other reports say about 40,000.
Coding notes: [E093] The maintainer's token explanation is reported via SecurityWeek, not a first-party post. Execute commands is coded from the RAT capabilities in Aikido's analysis. No victim activity was reported, so behaviours are NR. The payload is linked to the later react-native-aria campaign (E091). Tier set to 3 and Deploy software Y under decision 17 (malicious code delivered to customer endpoints through the supplier's own package, update or installer channel), 2026-11-26.

Access path: Attacker logged into legacy Cerner servers not yet migrated to Oracle Cloud, using compromised customer credentials, from about 22 Jan 2025 (detected 20 Feb 2025), and copied EHR data of multiple hospital customers to a remote server
Orgs reached (as reported): Multiple US hospital/health-system customers. The count is not confirmed in primary sources: news says at least 29 health systems, and litigation filings say about 80 hospitals. Eight health systems are co-defendants in the class action.
Primary source: https://oag.ca.gov/system/files/EXP_SampleIndividual%20Letter_1_Redacted.pdf ; Texas AG data breach report filed by Cerner Corporation (published 2 Oct 2026)
Coding notes: [E137] Entry used customer credentials, but the breached system was the vendor's shared legacy server, so this counts as a provider-held data breach. Exfiltration rests on Oracle's customer notice as reported by news. Oracle has not publicly confirmed totals. Extortion by an actor calling himself 'Andrew' is from news only. The number of customers is unclear, so the reach band is conservative.
People or orgs exposed: 19,929,149 individuals (Texas AG filing by Cerner, 2 Oct 2026)

Access path: Hacking of third-party administrator systems and files (Feb 2022 incident; second Dec 2022 incident)
Orgs reached (as reported): Multiple self-funded plan/flex/risk-pool clients; exact number not disclosed (State AG notices, HHS OCR)
Coding notes: [H005] Two separate hacks (Feb 2022 incident reported 2022-06; Dec 2022 incident reported 2023-02) share one HHS group. AG pages returned 403; relied on search snippets. Individual counts conflict (163k-186k). No techniques reported.
People or orgs exposed: 185,459 individuals (HHS, 2023-02-08 second incident) plus 172,450 (HHS, 2022-06-09 first incident); HHS group total 357,909 incl. 1,268 phishing 2025

Access path: Ransomware attack on a portion of Alvaria's hosted customer environment (9 Mar 2023 per California notice)
Orgs reached (as reported): At least 2 named customers (Shasta Community Health Center, Carrington Mortgage); HHS lists 6 reports by Alvaria (HHS, 2023-05-26)
Coding notes: [H035] Separate Nov 2022 Hive attack hit employee data; HHS rows relate to the Mar 2023 customer-environment incident. Notice PDF unreadable via fetch; facts from search snippets. Relevance kept General; hosted but not clearly IT/MSP service. Reach band is a floor.

Access path: Unauthorised third-party access to ApolloMD network, 22-23 May 2025
Orgs reached (as reported): 11 covered-entity clients named in ApolloMD notices (via HIPAA Journal summary)
Primary source: HHS OCR breach portal (ApolloMD Business Services, LLC, 2026-02-10)
Coding notes: [H047] Year set to first public disclosure (client/patient notices Jul-Sep 2025), not HHS posting in 2026. Qilin claimed it but ApolloMD did not confirm ransomware, so NR. 11 clients is 'Dozens' band by definition (10-99). Own notice not fetched.

Access path: Intrusion 20 Aug-1 Dec 2020, ransomware encryption 10 Dec 2020, data theft confirmed 24 May 2021
Orgs reached (as reported): Multiple employer/benefit plan clients; number not disclosed (AG notice, HHS)
Primary source: https://maine.gov/ag/attachments/985235c7-cb95-4be2-8792-a1252b4f8318/36b0a9a6-30c4-4942-9095-aaf86cfba741/eebb91ba-baca-4b6d-a159-3a63996e166e/Bansley- ME App & Sample.pdf ; HHS OCR breach portal
Coding notes: [H075] Maine/HHS pages not fetched (403/snippets only). Notice letters did not name ransomware, but HHS entry did. Counts conflict: ~274,000 (press) vs 91,763 HHS sum. Multi-customer based on payroll compliance for plans; classification of exact clients unnamed.
People or orgs exposed: 91,763 individuals (sum of 4 HHS rows, 2021-12-03); press reports ~274,000

Access path: Unauthorized access to one endpoint/server in Blue & Co's environment around 7 Nov 2024 (under 30 minutes); data removed. HHS describes an employee email phishing scheme.
Orgs reached (as reported): Information provided to Blue by 'certain companies' (number not stated); HHS 591,713 individuals (HHS, 2025-02-07)
Coding notes: [H092] The Mass AG page returned 403; facts come from search snippets of the notice. The HHS 'phishing' account differs from the notice's endpoint-access wording. The number of client companies is not stated. The accounting-firm role is not IT or MSP.

Access path: A Choice Health database was left internet-accessible by a third-party service provider's misconfiguration (Boru, Inc. named in one notice). An unauthorized party took files around 7 May 2022 and offered them for sale.
Orgs reached (as reported): Several carrier partners reported by name (Humana, UnitedHealthcare, Anthem); exact number not stated
Coding notes: [H122] The exposure came from a misconfiguration, not an intrusion technique; the attacker's method is not reported. The initial belief that only lead-generation data was affected was later corrected to include carrier partners' data. Counts differ: Humana reported 22,767 and HHS rows 14,307 to 46,371. The notice PDFs were not fetched, so this relies on search snippets and HIPAA Journal.
People or orgs exposed: 46,371 individuals across HHS entries (HHS, 2022); Humana alone 22,767

Access path: Unauthorized third party accessed the Compumedics USA network and copied files (15 Feb to 23 Mar 2025); entry method not reported. VanHelsing ransomware group claimed it, but Compumedics has not confirmed this.
Orgs reached (as reported): 11 healthcare provider clients named in notification (HIPAA Journal, 2025)
Coding notes: [H135] Eleven named clients is 10 to 99, so band is Dozens, though only just. Access dates conflict across sources (15 Feb to 23 Mar versus 13 to 24 Mar). The ransomware claim is attributed to the gang and not confirmed by Compumedics, so Ransomware is NR. Northern Light says none of its systems were compromised. Relevance is not MSP, as this is a clinical technology vendor.

Orgs reached (as reported): Sentra: 'more than a dozen' / 'dozens of Qubole customers'; Wiz: multiple victim AWS environments, no count

Incident: Railway platform breach exposed linked-account tokens

Orgs reached (as reported): 1,852 users' GitHub OAuth/BYOK tokens decrypted. Up to 1.85% of about 100,000 workspaces (about 1,850) may have had environment variables decrypted (Railway, Nov 2026). About $740K in fraudulent AI-token spend.
Coding notes: [E152] Incident ran Oct 20-21, 2026, so Year is 2026, not the pre-assigned 2025. MSP-specific because Railway is a hosting/cloud-infrastructure provider whose customers were reached. Lateral movement was inside Railway's infrastructure. Attacker dummy accounts were on Railway, not in customer environments. Access path could also be coded Build or release pipeline.
People or orgs exposed: 1,852 users (tokens), upper bound about 1.85% of workspaces; Railway, Nov 10 2026
